subject: Clarify metering for long sessions & request for rounding grace

Subject: Clarify metering for long sessions & possible rounding grace

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency metrics looked great. Before we move to a pilot, procurement has a couple of technical billing questions we need cleared up so Finance can sign off. High level: how will Redwood meter and round usage for our long interactive sessions? A few concrete items:

- If a user has a single chat session that accumulates 120k tokens in the KV / context across the day, how is that counted against the monthly token bucket? Do you charge on the full 120k at once or in windows?
- If a session spans two billing periods (e.g., starts 11:50pm and continues past midnight), how is proration handled? Is the token accounting split by time or by request?
- Do you apply any minimums or rounding per request, and if so, can that be waived/adjusted for pilot customers? Even small rounding on large counts creates material delta for us.

We'd like an example calculation (short) and any policy exceptions you offer for pilots (billing grace, cap, credits). Procurement is asking for this to appear in the SOW if possible.

Attached: our procurement questionnaire (filled).

Thanks,
Emma Dawson
Director, Data Products
Nova Health

Subject: Re: Clarify metering for long sessions & possible rounding grace

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then an example and a proposed concession we can take to Finance.

Summary answers:
- Windowing: we meter tokens per request, but we also have a context-rollup that aggregates per conversational session for billing when customers enable session aggregation. By default you'll see per-request billing; with session aggregation enabled we roll tokens into the session and bill at configurable checkpoints (we can set 1-hour checkpoints for your pilot).
- Proration across periods: tokens are attributed to the checkpoint when they were generated. If a session crosses the midnight boundary and you have 1-hour checkpoints, the tokens generated before midnight are billed in period A and those after in period B. We do not split an individual request across days — attribution is checkpoint-based.
- Minimums/rounding: we round per billing checkpoint to the nearest token quantum (default quantum = 1 token). We have per-request minimums only for streaming micro-requests; for aggregated sessions minimums can be disabled.

Short example (pilot config: session aggregation ON, 1-hour checkpoints, quantum 1 token):
- User conversation accumulates 120,482 tokens between 10:15–15:40 with checkpoints at every hour. Billing attributes tokens to each hour window (e.g., 10:15–11:00 => 14,102; 11:00–12:00 => 25,300; ...). Monthly invoice sums windows across the month. Rounding impact at 1-token quantum is negligible at scale; the main delta customers see is from model variant fallbacks and KV caching differences.

Proposed concession for pilot (what we can put in SOW):
- One-month "rounding grace" where any rounding/quantum rounding delta is credited back for the pilot month (applied as a usage credit).
- If Nova signs a 12-month committed capacity within 60 days of pilot completion, apply a 15% discount applied to token charges for the first 6 months.

For transparency I've attached a quick workbook showing numeric examples and a sample SOW clause. If that sounds reasonable I'll loop in Ben for pricing sign-off and Marissa for AM coverage.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
